findings:
🔵 [tuple-inside-body-compat] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The controller tuple sits inside the boundary receipt digest body (deviation from the brief, justified: the persisted row is `{...body, at, digest}` and the only known verifier, campaign-boundary-receipt-e2e, re-derives by dropping at/digest, so old rows without the tuple and new rows with it both re-derive from their own bytes). Nothing in the diff compares a new digest to a value computed without the tuple. Excluded: a future verifier that rebuilds the body from known field names rather than from the stored row would break; none exists in the diff or in the surfaces named, so this is a note for whoever adds one.
🔵 [dispatch-digest-vs-receipt-equality] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `boundaryDispatchResultDigest` is computed once from `classifyBoundaryRejected(mutation)` (dispatch record) and once from `bound` (receipt). If `bound` later gains a git-derived `candidate_ref` via `boundaryGitCandidate` when the mutation lacks one, the two digests diverge; the audit only requires presence/canonical form, so terminal is unaffected and test B's equality holds for the candidate-bearing fixture. Excluded from this version as it does not block the spec'd outcome; a one-line `const bound = classifyBoundaryRejected(mutation)` hoisted above the dispatch record would make the shared derivation explicit.
🔵 [pre-fix-parked-ledgers] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Campaigns parked in BOUNDARY_REJECTED before this change keep a null `result_receipt_digest` on the already-journaled boundary dispatch record and a tuple-less audit row; the unchanged audit still blocks them at terminalize. No migration is in the diff (correctly, per brief); the hand's report must state this.
